senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. רָצַע) [to perforate, cmp. הרג; חָלָל,] to slay, murder.
units: <cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 3:3">Midr. Till. to Ps. III</cite> (ref. to <he>ארבעתים</he>, <cite ref="II Samuel 12:6">II Sam. XII, 6</cite>) <he>אתה רָצַחְתָּ אחד שש עשרה נִרְצָחִים יהיו לך</he> thou hast murdered one: there shall be sixteen of thine murdered; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 148:4">Yalk. Sam. 148</cite>.

Macc. 12ᵃ מי כתיב אם ר׳ it reads not (Num. XXXV, 27), ‘if he slew’ (but, ‘he shall slay’); ib. מי כתיב יִרְצַח it reads not, ‘he shall slay’ (but, if he slays he is not punished); a. e.—Part. רוֹצֵחַ manslayer, murderer.

<cite ref="Mishnah Sheviit 10:8">Shebi. X, 8</cite>; <cite ref="Mishnah Makkot 2:8">Macc. II, 8</cite> <he>ר׳ שגלה … ר׳ אני</he> when an involuntary manslayer comes to his place of refuge, and the citizens desire to honor him, he must say, I am a manslayer.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 73a:5">Snh. 73ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 22:26">Deut. XXII, 26</cite>) <he>מקיש ר׳ … אף ר׳ ניתן להצילו בנפשו</he> the text draws an analogy between the case of one pursued by a murderer and that of the betrothed woman threatened with assault: as it is permitted to save the woman at the cost of the assailant’s life, so it is permitted to save the pursued at the cost of the would-be murderer’s life; <cite ref="Pesachim 25b:2">Pes. 25ᵇ</cite>; a. fr.—[<cite ref="Tosefta Sotah 15:7">Tosef. Sot. XV, 7</cite>, read: <cite ref="T00429"><he>רוֹצְעָן</he></cite>.]—Pl. <he>רוֹצְחִים</he>, <he>רוֹצְחִין</he>.
<cite ref="Makkot 9b:19">Ib. 9ᵇ</cite> <he>בגלעד שכיחי ר׳</he> in Gilead cases of manslaughter are frequent; a. fr.
<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 3:3">Midr. Till. to Ps. III</cite>; v. supra; a. e.

<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 24:1">Pesik. R. s. 24</cite> (ref. to <he>לא תרצח</he> <cite ref="Exodus 20:13">Ex. XX, 13</cite>) <he>לא תִתְרַצֵּחַ</he> thou shalt not murder thyself; [prob. to be read: <he>לא תִצָּרֵחַ לא תעשה הדם צוֹרֵחַ עליך</he> thou shalt not be cried about, make no blood cry out against thee].
